note: Suggested starting points for a daily drinks goal. People can always change them. Health reviewer must confirm before release.
food_share_note: EFSA's references are for total water, which includes the water in food. These suggestions assume food supplies about a fifth.

bands.label: 4 to 8
bands.why: EFSA's reference for ages 4 to 8 is about 1.6 litres of total water a day, including food. With about a fifth from food, that leaves roughly 1.25 litres from drinks.

bands.label: 9 to 13
bands.why: EFSA's reference for ages 9 to 13 is about 1.9 litres (girls) to 2.1 litres (boys) of total water a day, including food. That is roughly 1.6 litres from drinks.

bands.label: 14 to 17
bands.why: From age 14, EFSA uses adult references: about 2.0 litres (women) to 2.5 litres (men) of total water a day, including food. That is roughly 1.6 to 2.0 litres from drinks.

bands.label: 18 to 64
bands.why: India's NIN 2024 guideline describes about 2 litres of water a day, including other drinks, for a healthy adult, and more in hot weather or with hard exercise.

bands.label: 65 or older
bands.why: EFSA uses the same references for older adults as for other adults: about 2.0 to 2.5 litres of total water a day, including food. That is roughly 1.6 to 2.0 litres from drinks.

sources.title: EFSA Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for water (2010)
ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024, Guideline 14

medical_note: If a doctor has asked you to limit fluids, follow their advice and set that amount as your goal.
